info.title: Patch My PC Cloud Customer API
info.description: The Patch My PC Cloud Customer API lets you search and manage your applications, deployments, and deployment templates. Every operation except the token exchange requires an access token.

servers.description: United States. Use this host if your Patch My PC account is in the US region.
Europe. Use this host if your Patch My PC account is in the EU region.

post.description: Completes a new application creation process.

put.description: Completes an existing application update process.

post.description: Completes a new custom application creation process.

put.description: Completes an existing custom application update process.

post.description: Creates a new custom application draft.

put.description: Completes an in-place edit of an existing custom application version. Changes product metadata (display name, description, publisher, owner, developer, icon, and URLs) and update-level settings without creating a new version.

post.description: Creates a draft for editing an existing version of a custom application in place. Unlike an update draft, this doesn't create a new version—it opens the existing version for revision, so you can correct metadata without publishing a new version number.
Searches your own custom applications. Any feed types in the request body are ignored and replaced with `CUSTOMER`.
Creates a new update draft for an existing custom application.

get.description: Retrieves detailed information about an application in your custom application catalog. Returns only the fields relevant to a custom application.

delete.description: Deletes a custom application you own, freeing a slot against your custom application limit. Only your own custom applications can be deleted; public catalog applications are shared and can't be deleted. The request is rejected while the application's latest update is in a state that isn't safe to remove.

put.description: Completes an in-place edit of an existing application version. Changes product metadata (display name, description, publisher, owner, developer, icon, and URLs) and update-level settings without creating a new version. To publish a new version instead, use `PUT /v1/api/apps/complete`.

post.description: Creates a draft for editing an existing version of an application in place. Unlike an update draft, this doesn't create a new version—it opens the existing version for revision, so you can correct metadata without publishing a new version number.

Searches the public Patch My PC catalog. Any feed types in the request body are ignored and replaced with `PMPC`. `connectionId` is required and identifies the Intune connection that scopes the search.

get.description: Retrieves detailed information about an application in the public Patch My PC catalog. Returns only the fields relevant to a public catalog application. `connectionId` is required and identifies the Intune connection that scopes the lookup. `osType` is optional and defaults to `Windows`; `MacOS` requires your account to be entitled to macOS applications, otherwise the application is reported as not found.

post.description: Searches your custom applications using advanced filtering options. Any feed types in the request are ignored and replaced with `CUSTOMER`.
Creates a new update draft for an existing application.

get.description: Retrieves detailed information about an application in your custom application catalog by its product ID.

delete.description: Deletes a custom application you own, freeing a slot against your custom application limit. Only your own custom applications can be deleted; public catalog applications are shared and can't be deleted. The request is rejected while the application's latest update is in a state that isn't safe to remove.

get.description: Lists the Intune deployments that exist for an application under the given connection.

post.description: Creates a new Intune deployment for an application under the given connection.

get.description: Lists the existing deployments in the given connection that you can pick as a dependency for a new or edited deployment. Every deployment in the connection is returned; filter the results on the client.

Retrieves full detail for a single Intune deployment, including categories, Enrollment Status Page (ESP) profiles, and the dependency chain (parent and child deployments)—fields that the list operation doesn't return.

put.description: Edits an existing Intune deployment's name, group assignments, categories, ESP profiles, dependencies, and configuration—conflicting-process behavior, return codes, requirements, install parameters, application information overrides, and behavior settings. Any field you leave unset keeps its current value. Not supported for ring-enabled deployments.

delete.description: Deletes an existing Intune deployment. Allowed only while the deployment isn't in progress or already being deleted.

put.description: Forces a deployment to be recreated in Intune. Use it to troubleshoot a stuck or corrupted deployment; for routine version updates, use the sync operation instead.

put.summary: Set application deployment sync pause status
put.description: Pauses or resumes a deployment's scheduled sync.
Syncs a deployment to its latest pending version. Use it for routine version updates; to troubleshoot a stuck or corrupted deployment, use the redeploy operation instead.

get.description: Lists the files of an application's current version, in exactly the shape the completion operations accept. An edit replaces the file list rather than merging it, so you must send the complete list back; use this operation to get it without rebuilding it from local state.

post.summary: Exchange a personal access token for an access token
post.description: Exchanges a personal access token, supplied in the `Authorization` header as a bearer credential, for an access token that's valid for 60 minutes. Send the access token on subsequent requests, and exchange the personal access token again when the access token expires.

get.description: Lists the Intune connections available to the selected company. Use a connection's ID to scope application and deployment operations.
Retrieves information about your customer account, including its license and usage limits.

Lists the deployment templates configured for a connection, so you can find one and name it when you create a deployment. To author and change templates, use the create, update, and delete deployment template operations.

post.description: Creates a deployment template on a connection. Setting it as the default demotes the template that's currently the default.

get.description: Retrieves the settings that a deployment created from this template inherits.

put.description: Replaces the settings on an existing deployment template. Every field is stored as sent, so read the template first and change only what you need.

delete.description: Deletes a deployment template. You can't delete the connection's default template—make another template the default first.

bearerAuth.description: An access token from exchanging a personal access token at POST /v1/api/auth/token. Access tokens are valid for 60 minutes.
